newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 24.

text.p: Former Wool Board subsidiary Wool Services International is negotiating a wool-for-oil deal with Iran. However, Iranian ambassador Mohammed Sazgara said the deal -- potentially worth NZ$50 million -- was dependent on the involvement of the Dairy Board and the Meat Board. Sazgara said Iran did not want $50 million of wool, and would like to include meat and dairy products in the exchange. Page 1.

Alliance leader Jim Anderton has defended outspoken Alliance MP Pam Corkery's colourful maiden speech. Corkery did not drop her usual forthright manner for her speech, roundly criticising political opponents, using earthly metaphors and language to do so. However, Anderton said on Sunday that Parliament should not expect Corkery to act differently in Parliament. Page 2.

State-sector chief executives will in future be expected to resign if something goes badly wrong in their department, state services commissioner Don Hunn has said. Hunn said that after the Cave Creek platform collapse tragedy in April 1995, an accountability review being carried out by his office would lead to much clearer expectations about chief executives' responsibilities. Page 2.

Former speaker Peter Tapsell has said he would love to be high commissioner to London. London diplomatic sources were quoted last week as saying that Sir Peter was the leading candidate to be the next high commissioner. Page 2.

Ansett Australia's poor performance last year and concerns about the value of some aircraft have led Air New Zealand to cut the cash value of its investment in Ansett by $56 million. A A$60 million (NZ$66 million) slump in the value of Ansett Australia during a four-month period last year forced Air New Zealand to increase the goodwill component of the half share it bought for NZ$33 million. Page 17.

Direct Capital Partners made an after-tax profit of $3.65 million in the six months to December, slightly ahead of last year's $3.45 million. The specialist investor in small, unlisted companies said it would extend a share buyback programme from 1.75 million shares to 4.25 million at prices up to and including 75 cents. The latest result included a 42.8 million profit from the sale of a PC Direct stake. Page 17.

Max Resources said it had completed protracted negotiations to buy more organic fertiliser interests in exchange for five million fully paid 30 cent shares. The assets acquired included a half share in a plant that, when constructed, was expected to be the largest organic fertiliser making facility in the world, Max Resources said. Page 17.

Telecom can have its own facilities in the United States after gaining approval from the American Federal Communications Commission. "At the moment we are transiting traffic through the United States to other destinations, but we are now allowed to have our own facilities in the United States if we wish," Telecom's general manager of network marketing, Anthony Briscoe, said. Page 17.

A 7.9 percent rise in January home building figures showed a health continuation of growth in activity, Housing Industry Council chief executive Trevor Allsebrook said on Sunday. Figures issued by Statistics NZ last week showed that 1632 units were authorised in January, with Christchurch city up from 123 in January 1996 to 168, Tauranga district up from 80 to 123, Auckland city up from 97 to 125 and Banks Peninsula up from four to 30. Page 17.
